references.text: The Lord declares that he will take Israel as his people and be their God, and that they shall know that he is the Lord who brought them out of Egypt.
The introduction to the Ten Commandments where the Lord identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt.
The Lord reminds that he brought Israel out of Egypt to be their God, and that they must be holy.
The Lord declares that he brought Israel out of Egypt to be their God.
The Lord identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt to give them the land of Canaan and be their God.
The promise that the Lord will walk among his people and be their God.
The Lord remembers the covenant with the ancestors whom he brought out of Egypt to be their God.
The Lord declares that he is their God who brought them out of Egypt.
The promise that the Lord's dwelling shall be with Israel, and he will be their God and they his people.
The promise that the Lord will dwell among his people.
Paul quotes the promise that God will dwell among his people and be their God.
The fulfillment of the promise in the new Jerusalem where God dwells with humanity and is their God.
Prophetic reuse of the formula: God's identity as 'the one who leads' is now confirmed through the return from exile.
The foundation of the feast: The exodus is the historical event that establishes God's presence and is remembered in Israel's worship.
Concretization of liberation: 'To be their God' means to break the yoke and grant freedom from slavery.
Personal appeal based on historical salvation: God's past actions are the foundation for present demands of obedience.
